source: Vyasa and Vaishampayana: Critical Edition (BORI), Adi Parva 1.1.52–57 (Vyasa composed it and taught it to Vaishampayana, who recited it at Janamejaya's sacrifice). Ganesha as scribe: later tradition (the vulgate's Adi Parva 1, excluded from the Critical Edition), marked on screen.
structure: Every episode: RECAP (≈3 s, not in episode 1; KIT.series.recapStrip) → HOOK (one question; the episode title follows it: KIT.series.episodeTitle) → STORY → NEXT (a cliffhanger line, then the teaser card: KIT.series.nextTeaser).

voice.note: speaker → script/cast.json (voice, speed, pitch). Per line: speed (× the speaker's), pre/post (ms of silence before/after the voice, used by the timeline), say (what is spoken, if not `text`): '…' and '—' pause, ',' and '.' pause a little, [p:400] pauses 400 ms, {s:0.8} speaks what follows at 0.8× until the next {s:…} ({s} resets).

lines.text: Eighteen armies fought for eighteen days.
lines.note: RECAP: episode 3's eighteen army blocks on the field as a memory

lines.text: But who first gave this war its words?
lines.note: HOOK at the Naimisha fire: beats = 'who' (Sauti's hand opens to the smoke), 'words' (a palm leaf glimmers in it); the episode title shows in the post

lines.text: The sage Vyasa held the whole epic… in his mind.
lines.note: Vyasa's hermitage in the Himalayan foothills, morning. beats = 'Vyasa' (his name in gold), 'epic' (the verses kindle as lights around him)

lines.text: He needed a scribe. Ganesha agreed to write it — on one condition.
lines.note: traditionNote shows from here to the tusk (later tradition, not the Critical Edition). beats = 'Ganesha' (he is revealed, name in gold), 'one' (he raises one finger)

lines.speaker: vyasa
lines.say: Then write nothing… you don't understand.

lines.text: Whenever Ganesha paused to grasp a verse, Vyasa composed more.
lines.note: beats = 'paused' (the stylus lifts, he ponders), 'Vyasa' (new verses kindle above Vyasa)

lines.text: When his pen broke, Ganesha broke his own tusk… and kept writing.
lines.note: beats = 'broke' (the stylus snaps), 'broke' (he breaks off his tusk), 'kept' (he writes with it)

lines.text: Vyasa taught it to his disciple Vaishampayana, who first told it aloud at King Janamejaya's sacrifice.
lines.note: beats = 'Vaishampayana' (Vyasa gives him the bound manuscript; his name), 'King' (dissolve to the sacrificial fire of the king)

lines.text: But why was that sacrifice held?
lines.note: NEXT (cliffhanger). beats = 'why' (the smoke over the great fire coils like serpents), 'held' (the fire flares)
the teaser card, with a glimpse of episode 5 (Sarama)
